title: How Do Pilots Find Their Way?

scenes.title: How Do Pilots Find Their Way?
scenes.text: The sky has no roads and no street signs. So how do pilots know which way to go? Let's find out!

scenes.title: The Flight Plan
scenes.text: Before every flight, the pilots load a flight plan into the computer. It's a list of invisible points in the sky, called waypoints, joined up like a connect-the-dots puzzle.

scenes.title: Satellites
scenes.text: But how does the plane know where it is right now? Satellites! Dozens of GPS satellites circle high above the Earth. By listening to several of them at once, the plane works out exactly where it is.

scenes.title: Autopilot
scenes.text: Then the autopilot does the steering, flying from waypoint to waypoint. The pilots keep a close watch, and talk by radio with air traffic control.

scenes.title: Landing in Fog
scenes.text: Near the airport, the plane catches an invisible radio beam that leads straight down to the runway, like a guide rope. It works even in thick fog!

scenes.title: Remember!
scenes.text: Flight plan, waypoints, satellites, autopilot, and radio beams. That's how pilots find their way! See you on the next flight.
